etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English averren, from Old French averer, from Early Medieval Latin advērō, a verb derived from Latin vērus (“true”). Compare Modern French avérer.
senses: (ambitransitive) To assert the truth of (something); to affirm (something) with confidence; to declare (something) in a positive manner.
(ambitransitive, law) To justify or prove (an allegation or plea that one has made).

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From Middle English aver, avere (“workhorse; any beast of burden (?); things which are owned, possessions, property, wealth; state of being rich, wealth; ownership, possession”) [and other forms], and then either:
senses: (UK, dialectal, archaic) A beast of burden; chiefly a workhorse, but also a working ox or other animal.
